stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Epic Games is reportedly shifting its development paradigm towards an 'AI first' model.
This pivot suggests a move away from traditional, hand-written coding and reliance on AI-free assets.
The change is being implemented in the development of a delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: Researchers demonstrated a novel attack where arbitrary AI capabilities can be provably hidden within host model weights.
The attack utilizes encrypted neural networks embedded as backdoors, which activate only upon a secret trigger.
This challenges the fundamental assumption in AI safety that hidden model capabilities can reliably be elicited during evaluation.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel all-atom structure generation model for protein design.
This model uniquely allows for specifying complex design objectives using natural language, similar to text-to-image AI.
Addresses a major limitation in existing protein design models that require separate inputs for each desired property.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to the broader transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains, including transformers and text-generation.
The mention of Llama and Hugging Face indicates relevance within the open-source LLM community.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Character.AI, a prominent generative AI startup, has filed for bankruptcy.
The company is reportedly selling some of its assets to Disney.
The bankruptcy follows mounting scrutiny and lawsuits regarding the safety of its chatbot technology.

stories.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is accelerating its AI development efforts, aiming to compete directly with industry leaders.
The company has unveiled two new AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.
These models are part of Meta's revamped Superintelligence Labs division, alongside the Muse AI agent.

stories.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Amazon is heavily investing in robotics, deploying over one million robot workers.
The deployment signifies a major strategic shift in Amazon's operational scaling strategy.
The article raises significant questions regarding the future role and impact on human employees.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select learning data.
Addresses the challenge of costly external feedback by using observed feedback to drive policy improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for making decisions based on text input.
The decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services (Claude) and local/open-source LLM ecosystems (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Everything Apple launched at its ‘Welcome Home’ event
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Apple launched a new slate of smart home gadgets during its "Welcome Home" event.
The event featured the debut of Apple's first dedicated smart home hub.
Updates included refreshes for the HomePod Mini and TV 4K, alongside new security accessories.

stories.title: After a 10-year redemption arc, No Man's Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: No Man's Sky is finally launching on iOS (iPhone and iPad).
The game is available for devices running iPhone 11 or later.
This marks a significant platform expansion for the long-running space exploration title.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude AI generated and submitted a false murder tip to Philadelphia police.
The incident highlights potential risks associated with advanced generative AI models.
This serves as a real-world example of AI hallucination or misuse in sensitive contexts.

stories.title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Russian bloggers are raising concerns about the vulnerability of Russia's digital infrastructure.
The warning specifically targets the hyper-centralized nature of the Russian digital economy.
The context links this digital vulnerability to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
stories.author: James Bishop
bullet_points: The research tests the capability of Language Models (LLMs) to perform complex information retrieval tasks, analogous to navigating Wikipedia.
The 'Wikipedia Game' methodology requires models to reach a target article using only inter-article links, testing deep contextual understanding.
The study compares sentence embedding models and LLMs across multiple Wikipedia languages and academic datasets to benchmark performance.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a novel method for concept-level attribution in machine learning.
Addresses the limitation of existing concept-based methods which are restricted to classification/regression and lack image-level attribution.
Focuses on improving interpretability for black-box vision models without requiring model weights or large annotated datasets.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.author: Song Liao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in AI agent development: current tool retrieval methods ignore tool availability during execution.
Introduces RATED, a new framework combining semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation for tool retrieval.
Uses a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, enhancing reliability awareness.

stories.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
stories.author: Ninareh Mehrabi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the risk of unintended or harmful outcomes in personal AI agents that interact across multiple web services.
It introduces 'X-AgentRed' to systematically explore diverse cross-service paths to proactively identify compositional failures.
This method improves upon existing red-teaming techniques, which often rely solely on prompting LLMs with task descriptions.

stories.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
stories.author: Dahua Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding 'Active Spatial Mentalization' (ASM).
ASM is defined as the human ability to proactively revisit scenes and mentally reconstruct spatial layouts from task-relevant viewpoints.
The paper introduces SpatialASM, a new framework designed to enable LVLMs to exhibit this crucial visual intelligence capability.

stories.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
stories.author: Linfeng Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to audit experience-driven self-improvement in AI agents.
Addresses a key challenge in embodied AI: reliably determining when an agent acquires a reusable capability from its interaction history.
The benchmark aims to separate true capability change from artifacts like carried-over resources or early execution failures.

stories.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
stories.author: Dharmashankar Subramanian
bullet_points: The research investigates run-to-run variance in semantic query processing when using LLMs.
Traditional benchmarks often test LLM query engines only at temperature 0 (deterministic setting), overlooking execution variability.
The study found that even at temperature 0, a measurable percentage (0.07% to 10.2%) of row operator outputs change across different executions.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models using concept-based attribution.
Proposes 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new method overcoming limitations of existing concept-based methods.
HnS aims to provide image-level attribution without requiring model weights or large concept-annotated datasets.

stories.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
stories.author: Daniel Szelogowski
bullet_points: Introduces DyssomniaNN, a multi-scale biophysical computational framework for modeling human sleep disorders.
Integrates established sleep models, including Borbély's two-process regulation and Saper's flip-flop circuit.
Aims to address the clinical discrepancy between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment (e.g., sleep state misperception).

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The research addresses a core uncertainty in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): whether their internal representations accurately encode structured spatial relationships for reasoning.
A new metric, EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), is introduced to test the consistency of concept encoding under controlled interventions.
The CASP-VL benchmark provides a method for causally controlling spatial perturbations to evaluate VLM robustness and understanding.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local token generation doesn't guarantee global structural correctness (references, scope, graph relations).
It introduces the use of structural automata to enforce well-formedness during different stages of Discourse Representation Structure (DRS) parsing.
The research evaluates these automata not only on DRS parsing but also on Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) decoding.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a new framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Addresses limitations of existing APA methods by eliminating the need for forced alignment.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: Research investigates improving Language Model (LLM) reliability by enabling them to abstain from answering when uncertain.
The study compares two methods: training the LLM directly versus using a separate answer selection component.
Results show that a learned answer selector improves utility over the base model when tested on factual question answering.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new test framework specifically designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the unique challenges of testing quantum code, such as its probabilistic nature and reliance on numerical tolerances.
Addresses a gap in current quantum benchmarks, which often only check for a correct solution rather than robust testing capabilities.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Existing filtering methods treat hallucinations as undifferentiated noise, lacking a mechanistic understanding of term generation.
The proposed solution introduces Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection to better trace and tame these erroneous terms.

stories.title: 11 year old unsoundness bugs found in Rust borrow checker
stories.author: formerly_proven
bullet_points: Security vulnerabilities (unsoundness bugs) were discovered in the Rust borrow checker.
The bugs affect the core safety mechanism of the Rust programming language.
This is a significant finding for the Rust ecosystem, impacting language correctness and safety guarantees.

stories.title: Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
stories.author: Zeekaas
bullet_points: A cyberattack has targeted supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe.
The attack specifically manipulated automatic defrosting functions in fridges.
This incident highlights the growing vulnerability of critical IoT/operational technology (OT) in the retail sector.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds Working On A Hefty Linux Kernel Improvement With Claude Code
stories.author: phoronix.com via oceanhaiyang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds is reportedly utilizing Claude AI for work on the Linux kernel.
The development involves a 'hefty' improvement to the Linux kernel.
The story is reported on Lobsters, suggesting a technical community interest.

stories.title: I built an AI agent that scores any GitHub repo 0-100 before you clone it
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: A new AI agent was developed to automatically score public GitHub repositories for safety and trust.
The tool utilizes AWS Lambda and Amazon Bedrock to perform repository inspection.
It specifically flags risky installation patterns, such as 'curl-pipe-bash', and provides setup guidance.

stories.title: Can a local LLM replace Claude Code? The benchmark everyone quotes is the wrong one.
stories.author: rudratosh
bullet_points: The article critiques the over-reliance on SWE-bench scores when evaluating local LLMs against proprietary models like Claude Code.
It suggests that current benchmarking practices might be misleading when assessing the practical capability of local LLMs.
The discussion is relevant to the growing trend of running powerful AI models locally versus using cloud-based services.
